20261121-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.prompt: When a bag of snacks was carried up a high mountain, the snack bag swelled up tightly, as if about to burst. Which option explains the reason in terms of the relationship between gas pressure and volume?
20261121-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.explain: As altitude increases, atmospheric pressure decreases. The pressure of the gas inside the bag becomes greater than the outside atmospheric pressure, so the volume of the gas inside expands until the inside and outside pressures become equal.

20261121-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.hint.1: When the external pressure becomes smaller, the volume of the gas increases (Boyle's law).
20261121-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.o.o0: Because the higher you go up the mountain, the lower the atmospheric pressure (external pressure) becomes, so the volume of the gas inside the snack bag expanded

20261122-chemistry-m1-1.title: Advanced Diffusion Rate
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.goal: Apply principles of Advanced Diffusion Rate to solve the reasoning problem.
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.material: [Advanced Diffusion Rate] Cotton soaked in concentrated ammonia water (molecular mass 17) and cotton soaked in concentrated hydrochloric acid (molecular mass 36.5) were placed at the same time at the two ends of a long glass tube and the ends were plugged with rubber stoppers. After a while, a band of white smoke (ammonium chloride) formed inside the glass tube. Where is it located, closer to which end?
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Diffusion Rate] Cotton soaked in concentrated ammonia water (molecular mass 17) and cotton soaked in concentrated hydrochloric acid (molecular mass 36.5) were placed at the same time at the two ends of a long glass tube and the ends were plugged with rubber stoppers. After a while, a band of white smoke (ammonium chloride) formed inside the glass tube. Where is it located, closer to which end?
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.explain: The diffusion rate of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molecular mass. Ammonia gas, which is light with a molecular mass of 17, travels much faster than the heavier hydrogen chloride gas (36.5), so the two gases meet and react at a position closer to the hydrochloric acid cotton, where the relatively slower hydrogen chloride has moved less, forming the white smoke band.
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.hint.0: The lighter the gas molecules, the faster they diffuse (Graham's law of diffusion).
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.hint.1: Ammonia (17) is much lighter than hydrogen chloride (36.5).
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.o.o0: Closer to the cotton soaked in hydrochloric acid
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.o.o1: Closer to the cotton soaked in ammonia water
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.o.o2: Exactly in the middle of the glass tube
20261122-chemistry-m1-1.s.s1.o.o3: In the air outside the glass tube

20261118-chemistry-m2.s.s1.o.o3: Atoms are too small to carry an electric charge

20261119-chemistry-m2.s.s1.explain: An atom either loses electrons from its outermost shell to become a cation (mostly metals), or gains electrons to form an anion that satisfies the octet rule (mostly nonmetals).

20261119-chemistry-m2.s.s1.o.o3: The total number of electrons does not change when an ion forms

20261121-chemistry-m2-2.s.s1.prompt: To check whether chloride ions (Cl⁻), left in tap water as a disinfection by-product, are present, which reagent should be added, and what is the chemical formula of the white precipitate formed?
20261121-chemistry-m2-2.s.s1.explain: When the silver ions ($\text{Ag}^+$) in silver nitrate solution react with the chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) in the water, they form a white silver chloride ($\text{AgCl}$) precipitate that does not dissolve in water, so chloride ions can be detected.
20261121-chemistry-m2-2.s.s1.hint.0: When silver ions (Ag⁺) meet chloride ions (Cl⁻), a white precipitate that does not dissolve in water forms.
